profile.summary: PromoterAI is a deep learning model from Illumina that predicts how a variant in a gene promoter changes that gene's expression. It takes a list of variants (chromosome, position, reference and alternative allele, strand) and a reference genome, and adds a score between -1 and 1 to each variant: negative values mean lower expression and positive values mean higher expression. The authors built it to find noncoding promoter variants that may explain rare genetic diseases.

sections.title: How it works
sections.body: PromoterAI is a convolutional network written in TensorFlow and Keras. In the paper, a 20,480-base one-hot sequence is widened to 1,024 channels and passed through 24 MetaFormer blocks, each a depthwise convolution and a feed-forward step with batch normalisation and residual connections, with kernel size 5 and dilations chosen to cover 16,384 bases. The outputs of every fourth block are averaged to predict 970 human and mouse regulatory profiles over the central 4,096 positions. The model was first trained on these profiles around annotated transcription start sites, then fine-tuned on rare GTEx promoter variants with known expression effects; only the output layers, about 3 million parameters, were tuned. A variant's score is the alternative minus the reference prediction, averaged over positions and channels.

sections.title: Versions and reproducibility
sections.body: The paper's score is the average of two models: one trained and fine-tuned on human data only, and one on human and mouse data. The README's scoring command takes a single model folder and describes no averaging step. The Python package is at version 1.0rc6 in the repository read here. In June 2025 the authors said they had released the code and precomputed scores but not the model weights; in September 2025 they said the download link is sent by email after the licence agreement linked from the README is completed. The sources read do not name or version the distributed weights, so a result should name the package version, the repository commit, the model folder or folders used and the input length (20480).

sections.title: Scores and thresholds
sections.body: Scores run from -1 to 1. The README recommends cut-offs at 0.1, 0.2 and 0.5 in absolute value. Each variant row needs a strand; if it is unknown, the README says to create separate rows for each strand and aggregate the predictions. Precomputed scores for all human promoter single nucleotide variants are available for academic and non-commercial research after the licence agreement.

run_guide.summary: Install PromoterAI and score a small variant file against a reference genome, using a model folder obtained under the licence agreement.
prerequisites: Python 3.8 or later, with TensorFlow 2.13 to 2.15 and Keras 2 (installed by pip).
CPU or GPU; tested on H100 and A100 GPUs.
A trained PromoterAI model folder, sent by email after completing the licence agreement linked from the README. Noncommercial use only under the PolyForm Strict licence.
A reference genome FASTA file matching the variant coordinates.

steps.title: Prepare a variant file
steps.explanation: Writes two of the README's example variants to a tab-separated file with the required columns. Coordinates must match the reference FASTA used in the next step.

steps.title: Score the variants
steps.explanation: Runs the scoring command from the README. Replace path/to/model with the model folder received under the licence agreement and path/to/genome_fa with the reference FASTA.

quotes.text: promoterai \ --model_folder path/to/model \ --var_file path/to/variant_tsv \ --fasta_file path/to/genome_fa \ --input_length 20480

outputs: A copy of the variant file with a new score column, named by appending the model folder name to the variant file name.

notes: The existing source vep-uc-20261014-source-promoterai is the same README at the same commit. Weights access comes from collaborator replies on GitHub issues, not the README itself. The record's licence attribute says GitHub does not assert a licence; the repository LICENSE file is PolyForm Strict 1.0.0, which should replace that wording. A user on issue 15 refers to a model named promoterAI_v1_hg38_finetune; that name was not used here because no maintainer source states it. 'PolyForm-Strict-1.0.0' in the structured table is a short name: PolyForm Strict is not on the SPDX licence list (only PolyForm Noncommercial and Small Business are). Revision of 2026-11-27: the Science First Release full text is now read. The paper's ~208 million parameters is not put in structured, because no saved file says the distributed weights are that model. An email address on the earlier page was removed.
